body.statement: For the witness family, \[S_t=\{(7/8,s,9/8+2t):1\le s\le1+2t\}\quad(0<t<1/4),\qquad d_H(S_t,S_0)=1/4+2t,\] and with \(\pi_0=\pi_1=1/2\), \[\operatorname{KL}(P_{q_0},P_{q_t})=-\tfrac18\log(1-16t^2).\] For \(t_n=1/n\), the \(n\)-sample total variation distance vanishes while the sharp sets remain at Hausdorff distance tending to \(1/4\). Therefore no estimator is uniformly Hausdorff consistent on the model, and every uniformly \((1-\alpha)\)-honest random collection containing \(S(q)\) has Hausdorff diameter at least \(1/4-o(1)\) with probability at least \(1-2\alpha-o(1)\) along one of these laws.
body.justification: The causal discontinuity is converted into a statistical impossibility under fixed positive principal shares and fixed observed support.
body.gap: General uniform-inference papers motivate nearby-law analysis but do not provide this rank-similar set-separation experiment.
body.consumer: The lower bound prevents misleading globally shrinking policy-set error bars in Medicaid extrapolation.
